per_case_results.rendered_text: Brigatinib is a next-generation anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI).[1] Brigatinib demonstrates superior progression-free survival (PFS) over chemotherapy or crizotinib as first-line treatment for ALK-positive advanced non-smallcell lung cancer (NSCLC).[1] A completed Phase 2 clinical trial (NCT03535740) evaluated brigatinib in patients with ALK-positive advanced NSCLC who had progressed on alectinib or ceritinib.[2] The primary purpose of the Phase 2 trial NCT03535740 was to determine the efficacy of brigatinib by confirmed objective response rate (ORR) using RECIST criteria in participants with ALK+ locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC whose disease had progressed on alectinib or ceritinib.[2] The clinical trial record for brigatinib includes both first-line efficacy data in ALK-positive NSCLC and second-line efficacy data in patients who have progressed on prior ALK TKIs such as alectinib or ceritinib.[1][2]
The provided ChEMBL evidence for imatinib (CHEMBL941) does not contain a recorded alogp value.[1]
